clue.text: Ivy heard thunder around old shore

indicators.note: around means the anger word encloses the spoken letters

parts.note: to thunder is to rage, rant loudly

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: the name Ivy spoken sounds like the letters I and V

explanation.surface: A woman called Ivy hears a storm roll in over an old stretch of coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' means the name is taken as spoken: Ivy sounds like two letters, which 'around' puts inside the anger word. 'old' belongs to the definition, marking an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivage is an archaic, poetic word for a coast or bank, hence the 'old' in the definition.

clue.text: Sorry friends upset hotel being messy

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the words for sorry and friends are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: sorry in the sense of regretful or sad
pals are friends
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Apologetic friends are upset because the hotel room was left untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses SADPALS to SLAPDAS; H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hurried, so messy is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Go green after trouble at start of year

indicators.note: trouble as a verb means to disturb, so the letters of green are stirred up
at start of picks only the opening letter of year

explanation.surface: An instruction to adopt eco-friendly habits after a difficult start to the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges GREEN to ENERG; 'at start of' gives Y from year. 'Go green' looks like one phrase, but Go alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour or drive, as in 'full of go', a synonym for vitality.

clue.text: Poor reader initially held up — 'It's boring' …

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the assembled letters read from the bottom upwards
held means the first letter of reader is held inside the word for poor

parts.note: poor in quality means bad

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of reader

explanation.surface: A weak reader is stopped mid-performance and told the piece is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts R inside BAD to give BARD; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and colourless, a thing that is boring to look at or experience.

clue.text: … yes, Rob's struggling with fine school publication

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, as in a vote

indicators.note: struggling means the letters of Rob are thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Rob agrees but is finding the school's annual hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' scrambles the name to RBO; the 's after Rob reads as 'is', a link word. The ellipsis ties the surface to the previous clue only.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook is the annual record a school publishes of its pupils and events.

clue.text: Bum steer to statement's conclusion, in a way

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or wrong, so steer is a misleading arrangement of its letters
the conclusion of statement is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bad piece of advice steers a statement towards its end, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' rearranges STEER to STREE; T ends statement. 'Bum steer' is a set phrase for bad advice, hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road in a town, and way is a general word for a road or route.

clue.text: Sadly I'm old and rue becoming primate

indicators.note: sadly, as in badly or regrettably, signals the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A melancholy confession of ageing and regret on turning into an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges IMOLD and RUE together; 'and' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemuroid is a lemur-like animal, and lemurs belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Rail journeys home a little expensive — take alternative transport …

indicators.note: journeys suggests the letters of rail travelling about into a new order

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: a little of expensive is just its first letter

parts.note: R abbreviates recipe, Latin for take, in prescriptions

explanation.surface: Train trips home cost a bit too much, so the traveller tries something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journeys' rearranges RAIL to AIRL; 'a little' takes E from expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger plane is the other way to travel when the rail fare is too high.

clue.text: … course there's space on plane for one

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
the plane is one example of a tree

explanation.surface: Continuing the travel story: a meal is served with room on the aircraft for one passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the plane tree, not an aircraft; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served in a meal, so a course of dinner.

clue.text: Money passed over for a small dog?

indicators.note: passed over means the money word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: pay is money earned as wages
per means for, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Was money handed over to buy a little dog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed over' reverses PAY to YAP. The question mark flags that the definition is a description, not a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dogs are notorious for yapping, so one is jokingly described as a noisy barker.

clue.text: Wine in crate, red, lacking body — it's drunk in France

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the word for crate

parts.note: a box is a crate

indicators.note: lacking body means the middle of the word red is taken away

parts.note: eau is French for water, which is drunk

explanation.surface: Red wine packed in a crate, too thin to have much body, is consumed in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking body' strips E from RED to give RD; RD and EAU go 'in' BOX. 'body' in wine-talk misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is a French wine named after the region around the city where it is made.

clue.text: Maybe get broken into many bits

indicators.note: broken means the letters of maybe get are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Something might get smashed into lots of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' in the surface are fragments; in the definition they are binary digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A megabyte is a unit of computer storage containing millions of binary digits.

clue.text: Watching leaders leaving, doing as instructed

indicators.note: leaders leaving means the two front letters are taken away

parts.note: obeying is doing as one is told

explanation.surface: Someone watches the bosses depart while following orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders leaving' drops OB, the first two letters, from OBEYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying, a variant spelling of eyeing, means looking at or observing closely.

clue.text: Month with French king is duty

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A tax levied in a particular month under a French monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An octroi is a local tax on goods entering a town, a kind of customs levy.

clue.text: Promise unwilling head's not kept

indicators.note: head's not kept means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: loath means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: A reluctant headteacher's pledge was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's not kept' removes L, the first letter of LOATH.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn vow or pledge, as when sworn in court.

clue.text: I sometimes employ them when animals are trapped

indicators.note: are trapped means the two animals are caught inside the word for when

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a nag is a horse and a ram a sheep, two animals

explanation.surface: The setter speaks: certain devices come into play whenever creatures are caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are trapped' puts NAG and RAM inside AS. The 'I' is the setter, who uses this wordplay device; 'animals' suggests a letter-mix of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters regularly build clues from rearranged letters, so this is the device a compiler uses now and then.

clue.text: Run into writer, Kelvin — a grand fellow

indicators.note: into means the run letter goes inside the pen name

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Bumping into an author called Kelvin, who turns out to be a splendid chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside BIC; K follows. 'writer' looks like an author but is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a brick is an old-fashioned compliment for a reliable, good-hearted person.

clue.text: Programme I turn over outside room

indicators.note: outside means the turn and over letters go around the I

parts.note: a bend is a turn in a road
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A person flips a mattress outside the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts BENDO around I to give BENIDO; RM follows. Benidorm is a British TV sitcom set in the Spanish resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Benidorm was a long-running ITV comedy series, so a television programme.

clue.text: Pop a nasty piece of work at the start

indicators.note: at the start means the nasty person goes in front of the a

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: A nasty individual is shown up right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' puts SOD in front of A. 'Pop' looks like a verb or a father but means a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is an informal word for a fizzy soft drink, and soda is another such fizzy drink.

clue.text: Profile of naughty wives I'd ultimately like to go through

indicators.note: to go through means the letter from like passes into the mixed letters
naughty means the letters of wives and I'd misbehave and change places
ultimately takes the final letter of like

explanation.surface: An account of misbehaving wives that the narrator would finally enjoy reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles the fodder to SIDVIEW; 'ultimately' supplies E, and 'to go through' threads it into that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is the outline of a face seen from one flank, which is a view from the side.

clue.text: Can girl put in colouring ingredient?

indicators.note: put in means the girl's name is placed inside the can

parts.note: a tin is a can
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A question of whether a girl can add some dye to the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb asking permission, but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannin gives tea and red wine their brown tint and is used in dyes and inks.

clue.text: Saunas busted in capital

indicators.note: busted means broken, so the letters of saunas are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Police raid steam rooms in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busted' suggests a police raid but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Record of achievement

parts.note: the clue looks like a written certificate of success, but means a framed disc awarded for high sales

explanation.surface: A document listing what someone has accomplished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a written record but means a vinyl record, awarded to mark big sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians receive a framed gilt disc when a single or album reaches a sales milestone.

clue.text: Country going through after former finalist lost

indicators.note: after means the former word comes first and the route word follows
finalist lost means the final letter of the former word is lost

parts.note: late means former, as in 'the late president'
via means by way of, going through

explanation.surface: A country passes through after a team that once reached the final is knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalist lost' is read as 'final is lost': the last letter E goes, leaving LAT. 'finalist' looks like a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic nation in northern Europe.

clue.text: Look round the whole tree

indicators.note: round means the look word goes around the whole

parts.note: to see is to look
all means the whole

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk round and inspect an entire tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Sallee is an Australian name for certain eucalyptus and acacia trees, rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallee is an Australian eucalyptus, a kind of gum tree, also spelt sally.

clue.text: Reads badly to vintage campaigner

indicators.note: to means the mixed letters are attached to the vintage word

parts.note: cru is a wine term for a vineyard or its growth, a vintage

indicators.note: badly means the letters of reads are put in poor order

explanation.surface: Someone reads poorly from an old text to an activist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges READS to SADER; 'to' adds it to CRU.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader fights vigorously for a cause, a determined campaigner or activist.

clue.text: Gets worse — holds up banks

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the held letters read from bottom to top
holds means the answer is held within the letters of gets worse

explanation.surface: Things deteriorate when the banks hold up payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds SWOR across 'gets worse'; 'up' reverses it. 'Gets worse' looks like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks of seats or switches are tiers or lines, the same as rows.

clue.text: Nice you largely rate Polynesian islands

parts.note: tu is the familiar French for you, as spoken in Nice

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, the last letter dropped

parts.note: to rate something is to value it

explanation.surface: Telling someone that they rate highly in a nice way, on a Pacific holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so its 'you' is TU; 'largely' cuts E from VALUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuvalu is a Pacific nation of atolls in Polynesia.

clue.text: Look after current politician causing damage

indicators.note: after means the look word comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
MP is a Member of Parliament
an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A politician tends to the power supply and ends up wrecking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as one phrase meaning tend, but it splits: 'Look' gives letters and 'after' places them last.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, so to damage it.

clue.text: A short time after Easter, Frenchman returns cleaner

parts.note: Whit, short for Whitsun, is the festival seven weeks after Easter

indicators.note: returns means the French name is read backwards

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

explanation.surface: Soon after the Easter holiday a Frenchman comes back to do the cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the French name to ENER. Whitsun falls seven weeks after Easter, and 'short' cuts it to its first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitener is a product that brightens or bleaches things, a kind of cleaning agent.
